title: Annual Salary Calculator Australia: Convert Hourly to Yearly Pay with State Comparisons
description: Use our annual salary calculator Australia to convert your hourly rate to yearly pay. See how state differences in ordinary-time earnings affect your estimate.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, your annual salary is your hourly rate multiplied by 52 weeks, before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. Our calculator assumes a standard 38-hour week, but you can adjust the hours if needed. The result is your gross annual pay before tax and super.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include casual loading?
faqs.a: Yes, there is a checkbox that adds 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate you enter. Never type a rate that already includes casual loading; always enter the base rate first.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries or occupations. Our calculator uses the National Minimum Wage as a reference, but your actual rate may be higher under an award.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Use the Annual Salary Calculator Australia

Our **annual salary calculator Australia** helps you turn an hourly rate into a yearly figure. Simply enter your base hourly pay, and the calculator does the rest. It assumes a standard 38-hour week, which is the full-time ordinary hours under the Fair Work Act. If you work different hours, you can adjust the weekly hours field. The formula is straightforward: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks.

### Fortnightly Pay

Your fortnightly pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For a 38-hour week, that’s your hourly rate × 38 × 2. Many employers pay fortnightly, so this figure can help you budget.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage, which from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets a higher minimum. Award rates vary by industry and role. Our calculator uses the National Minimum Wage as a baseline, but you should check your specific award or agreement for your correct rate. See our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for more details.

## Casual Loading

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. Our calculator has a checkbox that adds this loading automatically. **Important:** always enter the base rate (the rate before loading) in the hourly field. Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading. The calculator will add the 25% for you. Learn more on our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

## Superannuation

Super guarantee is currently 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year. Our calculator estimates super at 12% of your ordinary earnings, stopping at that cap. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution your employer makes. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for details.

## Tax and Medicare

We use the 2026–27 resident tax rates: nil tax on the first $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Our calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. This is an estimate only. For a more precise calculation, use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool.

## State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Ordinary-time earnings vary across states and territories. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, the national average for full-time adult ordinary time earnings was $2083.70 per week in May 2026. However, this average masks differences: for example, workers in mining-heavy states often earn more, while those in retail-heavy states may earn less. Our calculator uses the national average as a reference, but your actual earnings may differ depending on your location and industry. For state-specific averages, refer to the [reference tables](/data) on our site. The ABS also reports all employees total earnings (including part-time) at $1579.20 per week nationally.

## Limitations of This Calculator

This calculator provides an estimate only. It assumes the same hourly rate every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It does not deduct HELP loans, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, and stops at the maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Always consult a qualified professional for your specific situation. For more detailed comparisons, see our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

## Why Use Our Annual Salary Calculator Australia?

Whether you are negotiating a salary or comparing job offers, our **annual salary calculator Australia** gives you a quick, reliable estimate. It accounts for the key differences between minimum wage, award rates, and casual loading. By understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, you can make informed decisions about your income.
